verdicts.explanation: The homepage's initial HTML carries only the title text and a meta-refresh to /nojs/splash; there is no rendered content for a non-JS fetcher to read.
The homepage carries no JSON-LD sameAs links to an external profile (Wikidata, Wikipedia, a verified social profile), so nothing anchors the Duolingo entity beyond its own domain.
Eleven course pages, each for a different language, share the identical generic title 'Duolingo' instead of a title naming the course, so a title-only reader cannot tell them apart.
The homepage's viewport meta tag sets user-scalable=no, which blocks pinch-zoom on browsers that still honour the directive.

fixes.quote: Duolingo Chess - Play Games - Learn Chess Online - For Free
site_specific: Serve the page's real heading, intro paragraph and chess-lesson list as HTML in the initial response, instead of only the title tag and a meta-refresh to /nojs/splash.
Keep the client-side app for interaction, but render the same text server-side so a non-JS fetch of /chess returns more than the title.
Add Organization or WebSite JSON-LD to the homepage's initial HTML response, including name, url and logo, rather than relying on the client-rendered app to add it.
Verify the tag is present in the server-rendered response, not only after JavaScript runs.
